March 2026

If you watch how people do their best work, a pattern shows up. The work happens in long stretches when nobody needs anything from them, and the stretches are rarer than they think.

Partly this is about attention. A single interruption costs more than the minute it takes, because it replaces the problem you were holding in your head with a smaller one. It takes a while to load the big problem back in.

So the question is not how to work harder. It is how to protect the hours when the big problem is already loaded. Most of the advice here follows from that.

Mornings

The easiest quiet hours are the early ones. Other people are asleep, and so is your inbox. You don't have to win any arguments to get them; you only have to go to bed earlier.

Notes

[1] This is less true for work that is mostly coordination.
